fatal_errors: Chemical substitution, particularly Co/Cr substitution, was not part of the target intervention or alloy system.
The hypothesis omits the experimentally important tuning methods of elastic tensile strain and nanoribbon spacing.
It predicts shifts in magnetic transition temperature, whereas the reported strain response preserved the approximately 70 K blocking peak.
The cited evidence concerns B2/BCC phase decomposition in different Al-based HEAs and does not establish magnetocaloric enhancement or low-dimensional behavior.
The cited Co-to-Cr substitution reduced saturation magnetization and promoted two-phase decomposition, conflicting with the claimed enhancement without phase separation.
explanation: The response partially recovers annealing-induced local atomic ordering as a way to modify exchange interactions and increase magnetic entropy change. However, it replaces the specific Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 thin-film/nanoribbon system with an unsupported generic composition-tuning proposal and misses the roles of 700 K structural relaxation, internal-strain relief, elastic tensile strain, and ribbon-spacing-dependent coupling. Its baseline and proposed measurements are usable but generic. Most importantly, the sole citation does not support the magnetocaloric claim and instead reports phase decomposition and reduced magnetization after Co-to-Cr substitution.
